name: International Space Station
location: Low Earth orbit, about 400 km up
evacuation: Return to Earth in about 6 to 24 hours in the docked crew vehicle.

healthFocus.title: Bone and muscle loss
healthFocus.detail: In weightlessness bones and muscles are barely loaded. Daily resistance and treadmill exercise is the main protection.

healthFocus.title: Fluid shift, head pressure and vision
healthFocus.detail: Body fluids move towards the head: a puffy face, a blocked nose and, over months, eye changes. Report any change in vision.

healthFocus.title: Cabin air (CO₂)
healthFocus.detail: Carbon dioxide can build up where air does not move. Headaches and poor concentration can be a sign; check the cabin reading.

healthFocus.title: Radiation, partly shielded
healthFocus.detail: Earth's magnetic field still blocks much of the radiation, but doses are higher than on Earth, especially when crossing the South Atlantic Anomaly.

disclaimer: Illustrative values for the prototype; replace with mission-approved values.
